overview: This House resolution sets the ground rules for debating H.R. 77, a bill that would let Congress use a single vote to overturn several federal agency regulations issued in the final months of an outgoing presidential administration (often called "midnight rules"). Resolutions like this one, known as "rules," decide how a bill is handled on the House floor. This one allows one hour of debate split between the leaders of both parties on the Judiciary Committee, waives procedural objections to the bill, and allows one "motion to recommit," a last chance for opponents to try to send the bill back to committee. The House adopted it on February 11, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule allows a timely vote on a bill to give Congress a more efficient way to review last-minute regulations from a departing administration.
against: Critics say the rule limits debate to one hour and blocks amendments from the floor, giving lawmakers little chance to change the bill.
